ledeLeadHtml: Phosphorus chemistry, levered to the semiconductor cycle:
ledeHtml: Rasa Industries, Ltd. (4022, TSE Prime; formerly Rasa Kogyo) - is the Tokyo-based chemicals group founded in 1913 on phosphate rock from  -  - Rasa Island, today organised into three reportable segments — Chemicals (phosphoric acid and phosphorus compounds, water-treatment coagulants and high-purity chemicals for electronics; 83.7% of FY3/26 external sales), Machinery (tunnelling machines, crushers, waste-treatment machinery, cast steel and precision machining) and Electronic Materials (high-purity inorganic materials for compound semiconductors and radioactive-iodine adsorbents) — plus a small, highly profitable Other business (petroleum-refining catalyst regeneration and real-estate leasing). The initiation question is whether FY3/27's step-up is a semiconductor-materials re-rating or a one-cycle spike in a single product. The exposure is unusually concentrated: semiconductor-related sales were 51.1% of FY3/26 revenue (¥24,369mn) and semiconductor-grade high-purity phosphoric acid alone 35.2% (¥16,796mn), with TSMC at 13.8% of sales (company securities report, via the interview pack). H1 FY3/27 printed revenue of ¥28,782mn (+26.8% YoY) and operating profit of ¥3,463mn (+21.1%), and on 4 November 2026 the company raised full-year guidance to revenue ¥62,000mn and operating profit ¥7,400mn (company guidance). Strengths: (1) a dominant, hard-to-qualify position in high-purity phosphoric acid into the AI/data-centre semiconductor capex cycle, with Chemicals earning ¥5,531mn of segment profit in FY3/26 (13.8% margin) and Electronic Materials growing sales 52.1% that year at a 29.1% margin on InP-related demand; (2) a balance sheet that has been rebuilt over the decade — equity ratio 34.3% in FY3/17 to 63.7% at FY3/26, interest-bearing debt down from ¥13,392mn (FY3/19) to ¥7,507mn, operating cash flow up to ¥6,149mn in FY3/26; (3) a stable profit ballast in Other (¥746mn of segment profit in FY3/26, a 63.4% margin) that cushions the cycle. Weaknesses: (1) concentration and input risk — one product is over a third of sales, the largest customer is 13.8%, and the main raw material, yellow phosphorus, is imported and price-volatile, so earnings hinge on volume holding and on cost pass-through keeping pace; (2) disclosure is thin — regional sales and profit are not disclosed at all (regions ND), there are no order, R&D or employee figures in the tanshin, no segment guidance, and no quantified mid-term financial plan exists against which to judge FY3/28 and beyond; (3) the rest of the portfolio is not growing — Machinery sales have fallen from ¥6,131mn (FY3/20) to ¥4,197mn (FY3/26), and Q2 FY3/27 standalone operating profit growth already slowed versus Q1. All historical figures are as reported by the company via the PL/segment sheet built from tanshin in the JPX disclosure archive (J-GAAP, March year-end, ten annual years FY3/17–FY3/26); the only forward figures are company guidance, labelled as such. No rating or price target is assigned at initiation (Under Review).

bullets.leadHtml: H1 FY3/27: revenue +26.8%, operating profit +21.1% — and a pre-announced raise that the print then matched.
bullets.html: For the six months to 30 September 2026 (J-GAAP), revenue was ¥28,782mn (+26.8% YoY), operating profit ¥3,463mn (+21.1%; margin 12.0% vs 12.6% a year earlier), ordinary income ¥3,604mn (+22.2%) and net income attributable to owners ¥2,518mn (+23.1%); basic EPS was ¥64.48 (post-split basis). H1 landed almost exactly on the revised H1 forecast issued on 4 November 2026 (revenue ¥28,700mn / operating profit ¥3,450mn). The quarterly split shows the momentum question: Q1 standalone printed revenue ¥13,709mn (+30.9%) and operating profit ¥1,805mn (+37.0%), so Q2 standalone (derived as H1 minus Q1, both as reported) contributed revenue ¥15,073mn and operating profit ¥1,658mn — growth decelerated even as the full-year guide was raised. Source: Q2 FY3/27 tanshin, 11 November 2026; Q1 FY3/27 tanshin, 12 August 2026.

bullets.leadHtml: Guidance raised once, by a fifth on operating profit — and H2 must accelerate.
bullets.html: Full-year FY3/27 company guidance (会社計画) was raised on 4 November 2026 to revenue ¥62,000mn (from an initial ¥54,000mn set on 14 May 2026), operating profit ¥7,400mn (from ¥6,200mn, +19.4%), ordinary income ¥7,600mn and owners' net income ¥5,200mn with EPS of ¥133.08; the dividend forecast was raised in the same notice from ¥36 to ¥43 per share (post-split basis). The Q2 tanshin of 11 November 2026 carried the revised figures unchanged. H1 delivered 46.4% of guided revenue and 46.8% of guided operating profit, so the guide implies H2 operating profit of ¥3,937mn (calculated), 13.7% above the H1 print, on semiconductor high-purity phosphoric acid demand in Japan and overseas and continued high levels of compound-semiconductor inorganic-materials sales, against rising main-raw-material costs (company-stated reason, revision notice of 4 November 2026). Source: revision notice, 4 November 2026; guidance tracker, 17 November 2026; Q2 FY3/27 tanshin.

bullets.leadHtml: Strength — Chemicals is the story: 83.7% of sales, and the semiconductor slice is the growth.
bullets.html: Chemicals' external sales were ¥39,956mn in FY3/26 (83.7% of consolidated revenue) with segment profit of ¥5,531mn (13.8% margin); in H1 FY3/27 its sales rose 28.8% YoY to ¥24,656mn and segment profit 16.5% to ¥3,158mn, on firm semiconductor-grade high-purity phosphoric acid in Japan and overseas and firm purchased-goods sales (company, Q2 tanshin). Semiconductor-related sales were 51.1% of FY3/26 group revenue and high-purity phosphoric acid alone 35.2% (securities report via the interview pack) — the segment is, in effect, a purified-chemicals supplier to the wafer-fab cycle, levered to AI/data-centre capex. Electronic Materials is the second lever: H1 FY3/27 sales +45.9% to ¥1,675mn and segment profit ¥619mn (37.0% margin) on compound-semiconductor demand. Source: Q2 FY3/27 tanshin segment note; FY3/26 tanshin segment note; interview pack (securities-report figures).

bullets.leadHtml: Weakness — the ten-year record is a long flat line with one spike, and disclosure gives no forward anchor.
bullets.html: Revenue was ¥23,283mn in FY3/17 and ¥28,978mn in FY3/21 — four years of drift — before the FY3/23 spike to ¥49,600mn (+40.1%, Chemicals-led) and the FY3/24 relapse to ¥42,788mn (−13.7%); FY3/26 revenue of ¥47,727mn is still below the FY3/23 peak, and operating profit has ranged between ¥1,622mn (FY3/17) and ¥6,012mn (FY3/26) with no stable trend. Against that record the company offers no quantified mid-term financial plan (the Mid-term Plan 2026 is in its final year and the tanshin discloses no numerical targets), no regional split, and no segment guidance — so the FY3/27 guide is the only forward anchor, and it is one year deep. Source: company results via PL/segment sheet (tanshin, JPX archive), FY3/17–FY3/26; sheet register S4/S7/S8.

bullets.leadHtml: Balance sheet and returns: the quiet improvement is real.
bullets.html: The equity ratio rose from 34.3% (FY3/17) to 63.7% at 31 March 2026 (total assets ¥49,973mn, net assets ¥31,840mn); interest-bearing debt fell from a decade peak of ¥13,392mn at FY3/19 to ¥7,507mn at FY3/26 against cash and equivalents of ¥4,823mn, and operating cash flow reached ¥6,149mn in FY3/26 — funding FY3/26 capital expenditure of ¥4,373mn (sheet definition: tangible fixed-asset acquisitions) internally. Dividends per share on the current post-split basis (calculated adjustment) rose from ¥8 (FY3/18–20) to ¥36 in FY3/26, and the FY3/27 forecast is ¥43 — a payout of about 32% of guided EPS and a 3.4% yield at ¥1,259 (calculated). ROE was 14.6% in FY3/26 as reported. Source: company results via PL/segment sheet; FY3/26 tanshin header; revision notice, 4 November 2026.

blocks.heading: 1. Key indicators and financial history
blocks.html:
Rasa reports under Japanese GAAP (J-GAAP), consolidated, with a March year-end. The history in this chapter and in Exhibit 1 covers ten annual years, FY3/17–FY3/26, as reported in each year's own tanshin, compiled in the PL/segment sheet for 4022 (main window FY3/22–FY3/26 plus the supplementary history block FY3/17–FY3/21 added in the H8 history-deepening wave; the sheet copy used is the LibreOffice-recalculated h8out copy — see Basis of preparation; all template checks equal zero, with documented rounding plugs of at most ¥2mn in the history block and ¥4mn in the main window). Per-share figures in Exhibit 1 are adjusted (calculated) for the 10-for-1 share consolidation of 1 October 2017 and the 5-for-1 share split of 1 April 2026 so that the series is comparable; as-reported per-share figures and the breaks are flagged in Chapter 9. Figures are ¥mn unless stated.

Revenue describes a long flat decade interrupted by one spike. Sales were ¥23,283mn in FY3/17 and grew to ¥30,999mn by FY3/19, then fell two years (¥29,759mn in FY3/20, ¥28,978mn in FY3/21) before recovering to ¥35,411mn in FY3/22 (+22.2%). FY3/23 then printed ¥49,600mn (+40.1%) — almost entirely a Chemicals event (segment sales +51.9% to ¥41,918mn) — and FY3/24 gave back part of it at ¥42,788mn (−13.7%). The last two years rebuilt steadily: ¥45,421mn in FY3/25 (+6.2%) and ¥47,727mn in FY3/26 (+5.1%), still 3.8% below the FY3/23 peak. Operating profit followed the same shape at higher amplitude: ¥1,622mn (7.0% margin) in FY3/17, ¥2,842mn in FY3/18, a FY3/20 trough of ¥1,871mn, then ¥3,475mn / ¥4,622mn / ¥3,591mn / ¥4,736mn across FY3/22–25 and a decade high of ¥6,012mn in FY3/26 (12.6% margin). The gross margin is the swing line: 24.4% in FY3/17, compressed to 19.1% in FY3/21, then rebuilt through 22.7% (FY3/22), 19.0% in the FY3/23 volume spike, 19.3% (FY3/24), 21.2% (FY3/25) and 23.0% in FY3/26 (calculated from reported sales and cost of sales) — mix toward high-purity semiconductor chemicals and price pass-through doing the work, on the company's own qualitative account. SG&A stayed in a narrow ¥4,073mn–¥4,948mn band across all ten years, so operating leverage is a gross-margin story, not a cost story.

Below operating profit the J-GAAP lines are small and clean by recent standards. Ordinary income tracked operating profit closely (¥1,342mn in FY3/17 to ¥6,191mn in FY3/26), helped in FY3/26 by equity-method income (¥337mn per the FY3/26 tanshin reference line). Extraordinary items were minor in the main window (FY3/26: income ¥0mn, losses ¥1mn) but not in the history block (FY3/17 extraordinary losses ¥190mn). One history-block item must be normalised before any trend is read: FY3/17 carried a deferred-tax credit of −¥749mn, so net income of ¥1,740mn exceeded profit before tax of ¥1,199mn and the reported ROE of 17.8% for that year is not an operating result. Net income attributable to owners was ¥1,729mn / ¥2,251mn / ¥2,274mn / ¥1,377mn / ¥2,004mn / ¥2,538mn / ¥3,232mn / ¥2,382mn / ¥3,131mn / ¥4,359mn across FY3/17–FY3/26, and reported ROE (owners' profit over average owners' equity, tanshin header) printed 17.8% / 19.0% / 16.4% / 9.1% / 12.0% / 13.4% / 14.9% / 9.9% / 11.9% / 14.6% — respectable throughout, because the equity base was small for most of the decade.

The balance sheet is where the decade's progress is unambiguous. Total assets rose from ¥31,310mn (FY3/17) to ¥49,973mn at 31 March 2026; net assets from ¥10,780mn to ¥31,840mn; the equity ratio from 34.3% to 63.7%. Interest-bearing debt (borrowings and bonds as presented, sheet definition) peaked at ¥13,392mn at FY3/19 and was cut to ¥7,507mn by FY3/26, against cash and equivalents of ¥4,823mn — a net debt position of about ¥2,684mn (calculated) that is modest against FY3/26 operating cash flow of ¥6,149mn. Operating cash flow itself stepped up from the ¥1,803mn–¥2,963mn range of FY3/17–21 to ¥1,996mn / ¥2,042mn / ¥4,972mn / ¥5,038mn / ¥6,149mn in FY3/22–26. Capital expenditure (tangible fixed-asset acquisitions, sheet definition) was ¥944mn–¥3,561mn a year in the history block and ¥2,430mn / ¥919mn / ¥983mn / ¥1,872mn / ¥4,373mn in the main window — the FY3/26 step-up coincides with the Taiwan capacity expansion discussed in Chapter 7 (the tanshin does not itemise capex by project). Exhibit 1 (page 1) gives the full KPI table including FY3/27 company guidance. Source for this chapter: company results via PL/segment sheet (tanshin, JPX archive), FY3/17–FY3/26; FY3/26 tanshin header, 14 May 2026.

blocks.heading: 2. Latest update — Q2 FY3/27 results and guidance
blocks.html: Rasa reported Q2 FY3/27 (H1, 1 April–30 September 2026) results on 11 November 2026, one week after the 4 November 2026 notice that raised the H1 and full-year forecasts and the dividend. The company publishes results briefing materials and holds a briefing for institutional investors and analysts (per the tanshin header), but there is no English transcript for 4022 in the programme's transcript library and no Q&A record is cited anywhere in this report (see Basis of preparation). This chapter summarises the release; segment detail is in Chapter 5.

blocks.heading: H1 FY3/27 results (cumulative, as reported)
blocks.html:
Revenue was ¥28,782mn (+26.8% YoY), operating profit ¥3,463mn (+21.1%; margin 12.0%, down 0.6pt YoY), ordinary income ¥3,604mn (+22.2%), interim net income attributable to owners ¥2,518mn (+23.1%) and basic EPS ¥64.48 (post-split basis; no dilutive securities are presented). Comprehensive income was ¥2,677mn. H1 landed almost exactly on the revised H1 forecast published on 4 November 2026 (revenue ¥28,700mn, operating profit ¥3,450mn, per the interview pack's record of the revision notice) — the raise was, in effect, pre-announced a week before the tanshin. The quarterly split matters for the debate: Q1 FY3/27 standalone (tanshin, 12 August 2026) printed revenue of ¥13,709mn (+30.9% YoY) and operating profit of ¥1,805mn (+37.0%), so Q2 standalone (derived as H1 minus Q1, both as reported) contributed revenue of ¥15,073mn (+23.2% on the derived prior-year quarter) and operating profit of ¥1,658mn (+7.5% on the derived prior-year quarter) — volume kept growing but profit growth decelerated sharply, the interview pack's central open question (cost, mix or shipment timing — the tanshin does not itemise the cause).

By segment (external revenue / segment profit, Q2 tanshin segment note): Chemicals ¥24,656mn / ¥3,158mn (+28.8% / +16.5% YoY) — semiconductor-grade high-purity phosphoric acid firm in Japan and overseas and purchased-goods sales firm, coagulants firm on waterworks demand, capacitor raw materials firm; Machinery ¥1,929mn / ¥110mn (+13.5% / +29.4%); Electronic Materials ¥1,675mn / ¥619mn (+45.9% / +76.3%) on compound-semiconductor high-purity inorganic materials; Other ¥521mn / ¥333mn (−26.1% / −19.9%). Corporate adjustments were −¥758mn, reconciling segment profit of ¥4,221mn to consolidated operating profit of ¥3,463mn. The H1 segment split is disclosed in full in the Q2 tanshin segment note — the interview pack, compiled from the tanshin summary, had marked it 未取得; this report uses the tanshin note and flags the difference in Chapter 9.

The balance sheet at 30 September 2026: total assets ¥52,474mn, net assets ¥33,637mn, equity ratio 64.1% (31 March 2026: ¥49,973mn / ¥31,840mn / 63.7%). Shares issued were 39,721,015 (post-split basis as printed in the tanshin, which restates share counts as if the 1 April 2026 5-for-1 split had occurred at the start of FY3/26), with 646,030 in treasury; the H1 weighted average was 39,065,101 shares. The interim dividend is ¥18 per share (post-split), with payment scheduled from 2 December 2026. Source: Q2 FY3/27 tanshin, 11 November 2026; Q1 FY3/27 tanshin, 12 August 2026.

blocks.heading: Guidance: raised on 4 November 2026 — revenue ¥62,000mn, operating profit ¥7,400mn (company guidance)
blocks.html:
Full-year FY3/27 guidance, as revised in the notice of 4 November 2026 and confirmed unchanged in the Q2 tanshin of 11 November 2026, is revenue ¥62,000mn (+29.9% YoY), operating profit ¥7,400mn (+23.1%), ordinary income ¥7,600mn and net income attributable to owners ¥5,200mn with basic EPS of ¥133.08 — company guidance (会社計画), J-GAAP, not a J-Core Fundamental Research forecast. The full chain, with dates, is: initial guidance published with the FY3/26 tanshin on 14 May 2026 (revenue ¥54,000mn, operating profit ¥6,200mn, ordinary income ¥6,300mn, owners' net income ¥4,300mn, EPS ¥110.08; H1 forecast revenue ¥26,000mn / operating profit ¥2,800mn; dividend forecast ¥36 per share post-split); Revision 1 on 4 November 2026 (revenue ¥62,000mn, operating profit ¥7,400mn, ordinary income ¥7,600mn, owners' net income ¥5,200mn, EPS ¥133.08; dividend forecast raised to ¥43); confirmed without change in the Q2 tanshin on 11 November 2026 (修正の有無：無 relative to the 4 November notice). The guidance tracker (17 November 2026) records exactly one revision, +19.4% on operating profit, dated 2026-11-04, and the sheet register agrees on the current figures (its shorthand 'unchanged at Q2' refers to the Q2 tanshin carrying the revised figures — see Chapter 9).

The company's stated reason (revision notice, 4 November 2026): in Chemicals, despite cost increases in the main raw materials for phosphoric acid, semiconductor-grade high-purity phosphoric acid is expected to perform firmly in Japan and overseas on the back of a firm semiconductor market and strong demand; in Electronic Materials, sales of high-purity inorganic materials for compound semiconductors are expected to remain at a high level; and the H1 progress plus these full-year prospects put the year above the previous forecast. No segment-level guidance is disclosed, and no FX or raw-material price assumptions are published in the tanshin — both are gaps for the H2 debate. Against the guide, H1 progress was 46.4% on revenue and 46.8% on operating profit, so delivery requires H2 revenue of ¥33,218mn and H2 operating profit of ¥3,937mn (both calculated), an H2 operating margin of about 11.9% — below the H1 margin of 12.0% but on 15.4% more revenue than H1, i.e. the guide is a volume step-up story concentrated in Chemicals. Exhibit 3 sets out the H1 actuals, the H1 segment detail and the full-year guidance. The monitoring yardstick for Q3 (expected February 2027) is the interview pack's: cumulative operating-profit progress against ¥7,400mn, Chemicals segment profit and the semiconductor-related sales ratio, and whether Electronic Materials holds above +50% YoY. Source: FY3/26 tanshin section 3, 14 May 2026; revision notice, 4 November 2026; Q2 FY3/27 tanshin, 11 November 2026; guidance tracker, 17 November 2026.

blocks.heading: 3. Business description
blocks.html: Rasa organises itself into three reportable segments — Chemicals, Machinery and Electronic Materials — plus Other (businesses not in the reportable segments: petroleum-refining catalyst regeneration, real-estate leasing and the like). The segment definitions below are the company's own (FY3/26 tanshin, segment note): Chemicals produces phosphoric acid and phosphorus-based secondary salts, water-treatment coagulants, high-function high-purity chemicals for the electronics industry, and deodorising/antibacterial agents; Machinery produces tunnelling machines, crushing machinery, municipal/industrial waste-treatment machinery, cast-steel products and precision machining; Electronic Materials produces high-purity inorganic materials and radioactive-iodine adsorbents. Segment profit is on the operating-profit basis, and the adjustment line is unallocated corporate expenses, mainly G&A and R&D not attributable to segments (segment note). In FY3/26 (external revenue basis) the mix was Chemicals 83.7%, Machinery 8.8%, Electronic Materials 5.0% and Other 2.5%; segment profit before the −¥1,366mn corporate adjustment (sheet basis; printed −¥1,367mn — Chapter 9) was Chemicals ¥5,531mn, Other ¥746mn, Electronic Materials ¥696mn and Machinery ¥405mn. The group's centre of gravity is therefore a single chemistry — phosphorus — sold into two cycles (semiconductor/electronics and public-works/construction), with a small leasing/catalyst annuity attached.

blocks.heading: Chemicals: phosphoric acid, from commodity salts to semiconductor-grade purity
blocks.html: Chemicals is the founding business and the group's engine. The product ladder runs from phosphoric acid and phosphorus secondary salts (fertiliser/industrial heritage) through water-treatment coagulants (aluminium-based, sold into waterworks — firm in H1 FY3/27 on waterworks demand) to the value end: high-function, high-purity chemicals for the electronics industry, above all semiconductor-grade high-purity phosphoric acid used in wafer processing, plus capacitor raw materials and deodorising/antibacterial agents. The financial profile is high-volume and mid-margin: external sales of ¥16,504mn / ¥19,459mn / ¥22,127mn / ¥21,089mn / ¥21,750mn in FY3/17–21, then ¥27,585mn / ¥41,918mn / ¥34,391mn / ¥38,168mn / ¥39,956mn in FY3/22–26, with segment profit of ¥1,451mn / ¥1,988mn / ¥1,795mn / ¥1,420mn / ¥2,192mn and then ¥2,980mn / ¥4,115mn / ¥3,028mn / ¥4,840mn / ¥5,531mn — margins of 8.8%–10.7% in the history block and 10.8% / 9.8% / 8.8% / 12.7% / 13.8% in the main window. The FY3/23 sales spike (+51.9%) and FY3/24 relapse (−18.0%) show how much of the segment is price- and cycle-sensitive commodity phosphorus volume; the FY3/25–26 margin rebuild to 13.8% is the mix shift toward high-purity grades. The demand disclosure that matters most sits outside the segment note: semiconductor-related sales were 51.1% of FY3/26 consolidated revenue (¥24,369mn) and high-purity phosphoric acid alone 35.2% (¥16,796mn), with TSMC the largest customer at 13.8% of sales (FY3/26 securities report, via the interview pack). H1 FY3/27 kept the run going: sales ¥24,656mn (+28.8% YoY), segment profit ¥3,158mn (12.8% margin). Production and capacity data (sites, tonnage, utilisation) are not disclosed in the tanshin and are not quantified in this report. Source: company results via PL/segment sheet (tanshin, JPX archive); Q2 FY3/27 tanshin; interview pack (securities-report figures).

blocks.heading: Machinery: tunnelling and crushing equipment — the shrinking second leg
blocks.html: Machinery builds tunnelling machines (notably sewerage-related boring machines, where rental units are a recurring element), crushers and related plant, municipal and industrial waste-treatment machinery, cast-steel products and precision machining. It is a domestic public-works and construction-cycle business, and it is shrinking: external sales of ¥4,273mn / ¥5,104mn / ¥5,441mn / ¥6,131mn / ¥4,409mn in FY3/17–21 became ¥4,766mn / ¥4,739mn / ¥5,584mn / ¥4,491mn / ¥4,197mn in FY3/22–26, and segment profit swung between ¥119mn (FY3/25, a 2.6% margin) and ¥630mn (FY3/20). FY3/26 detail (tanshin qualitative section): construction machinery weakened — crusher unit sales and plant sales were soft, partly offset by consumable-parts sales and precision machining growth — while civil-engineering machinery was firm on sewerage tunnelling-machine rentals and unit sales; the segment printed sales of ¥4,197mn (−6.5% YoY) and segment profit of ¥405mn. H1 FY3/27 recovered modestly (sales ¥1,929mn, +13.5% YoY; segment profit ¥110mn, a 5.7% margin). Machinery is 8.8% of sales and under 7% of segment profit: it diversifies the cycle (public works versus semiconductors) but no longer moves the group result, and no order intake or backlog is disclosed for it in the tanshin (未取得). Source: company results via PL/segment sheet (tanshin, JPX archive); FY3/26 and Q2 FY3/27 tanshin qualitative sections.

blocks.heading: Electronic Materials and Other: the small, high-margin growth option and the annuity
blocks.html:
Electronic Materials makes high-purity inorganic materials — above all feedstock materials for compound semiconductors (the InP chain that feeds optical-communications components for AI data centres) — and radioactive-iodine adsorbents, drawing on rare-metal recycling technology accumulated over many years (company president's message). It is small but the group's highest-growth, highest-margin reportable segment: external sales of ¥1,297mn / ¥1,641mn / ¥2,234mn / ¥1,364mn / ¥1,706mn in FY3/17–21 and ¥1,997mn / ¥1,830mn / ¥1,635mn / ¥1,574mn / ¥2,395mn in FY3/22–26, with segment profit of ¥108mn / ¥370mn / ¥575mn / ¥24mn / ¥400mn and then ¥424mn / ¥565mn / ¥368mn / ¥244mn / ¥696mn — margins between 15.5% and 30.9% in the main window (29.1% in FY3/26). FY3/26 sales rose 52.1% (the FY3/25 base included a one-off gallium spot sale whose absence the company flagged in its FY3/27 outlook commentary, making the FY3/26 growth the cleaner read), and H1 FY3/27 accelerated further: sales ¥1,675mn (+45.9% YoY), segment profit ¥619mn, a 37.0% margin — already 70% of the segment's full-year FY3/26 sales in one half. Whether this is a second pillar or a spike is one of the interview pack's live debates; order visibility and the binding constraint (indium/gallium supply versus own capacity) are not disclosed.

Other — petroleum-refining catalyst regeneration and real-estate leasing — is the portfolio's annuity: sales of ¥1,112mn–¥1,220mn in every one of the ten years (¥1,176mn in FY3/26) and segment profit of ¥688mn–¥764mn a year (¥746mn in FY3/26), a margin above 60% in every year of the decade (63.4% in FY3/26). It contributed 10.1% of FY3/26 segment profit on 2.5% of sales. H1 FY3/27 was the segment's first soft half in the record (sales ¥521mn, −26.1% YoY; profit ¥333mn) — worth a question, not yet a trend. Source: company results via PL/segment sheet (tanshin, JPX archive); Q2 FY3/27 tanshin segment note; company president's message (accessed November 2026).

blocks.heading: 4. Market and value chain
blocks.html:
Rasa sits at the materials layer of two value chains. In semiconductors, the chain runs from imported yellow phosphorus (the main raw material for phosphoric acid, whose procurement price the securities report flags as subject to sharp swings — 暴騰暴落 — via the interview pack) through Rasa's purification and formulation into high-purity phosphoric acid and high-purity inorganic materials, and onward to wafer fabs (etching/cleaning chemistry) and compound-semiconductor device makers (InP feedstock for optical transceivers). Demand is derived twice over: AI/data-centre investment drives leading-edge and mature-node fab utilisation and optical-link build-out, which drives chemical volumes. The company attributes the FY3/27 guidance raise to exactly this chain — firm semiconductor demand in Japan and overseas for high-purity phosphoric acid, and continued high levels of compound-semiconductor inorganic-materials sales — while also noting the offset: main-raw-material cost increases in phosphoric acid. The pass-through question (procurement price → product price, and the lag) is therefore the central margin variable, and it is not quantified in the tanshin. Customer concentration is the second structural fact: TSMC was 13.8% of FY3/26 sales (securities report via the interview pack) — pricing power and hostage risk in one number, and the direction of that share under the new guide is an interview question, not a disclosed figure.

In the domestic chain, Chemicals' coagulants sell into waterworks demand (stable, public), and Machinery sells tunnelling and crushing equipment into sewerage and construction spending — lower growth, but uncorrelated with the semiconductor cycle. Entry barriers in the growth chain are qualification and purity: a high-purity chemical written into a fab's process is sticky, purification know-how accumulated over a century of phosphoric-acid technology (the company's own framing) is the moat, and supply responsibility — the company's stated commitment to a production system that meets global demand, including the Taiwan expansion — is part of the offer. The substitute and share risks are the standard ones for a niche materials supplier: competing high-purity chemical makers qualifying at the same fabs, customer dual-sourcing against a 13.8% concentration, and the lumpiness of the AI capex cycle itself. No company-disclosed market-size or market-share figure for high-purity phosphoric acid or InP feedstock is carried in the sources used here, and none is substituted (未取得). Sources: Q2 FY3/27 tanshin; revision notice, 4 November 2026; interview pack (securities-report risk and customer figures); company president's message (accessed November 2026).

blocks.heading: Business segments: Chemicals carries sales and profit; Electronic Materials carries growth
blocks.html: Exhibit 2 gives the ten-year history on the basis disclosed in each year's own tanshin (external sales; segment profit on the operating-profit basis; adjustment = unallocated corporate expenses). Three facts organise it. First, profit concentration: in FY3/26 the four segments earned ¥7,378mn of segment profit before the corporate adjustment — Chemicals ¥5,531mn (75.0%), Other ¥746mn, Electronic Materials ¥696mn and Machinery ¥405mn — so the group's earnings power is a Chemicals margin question, and Chemicals' margin has printed 8.8%–13.8% across the decade with the two best years the most recent two. Second, the growth option is real but small: Electronic Materials' FY3/26 segment profit (¥696mn) already exceeded Machinery's (¥405mn) on 57% of its sales, and its H1 FY3/27 margin of 37.0% is the group's highest — but at 5.0% of group sales it cannot yet offset a Chemicals downturn. Third, stability sits in Other: ¥688mn–¥764mn of segment profit in every year of the decade at a margin above 60%, the closest thing Rasa has to a bond inside the P&L — which makes its H1 FY3/27 decline (−19.9% YoY) the half's quiet negative. There are no segment basis changes to flag in the ten years: the same three reportable segments plus Other are presented throughout, and segment profit is on the operating-profit basis in every year (register S3/S11). The only reconciling items are rounding: the printed corporate adjustments differ from the sheet's formula adjustments by ¥1mn–¥2mn in several years (Chapter 9). blocks.heading: 7. Strategy and shareholder returns — RasaVision2033 and Mid-term Plan 2026; no quantified mid-term financial plan
blocks.html:
The company's stated frame is the long-term vision 'RasaVision2033' (for the 120th anniversary of its founding) and, beneath it, 'Mid-term Management Plan 2026' covering FY3/25–FY3/27 (2024–2026 in the company's fiscal labelling), of which FY3/27 is the final year — the plan period is described in the Q2 FY3/27 tanshin as the 'seed-sowing' Phase 1 toward the vision. The plan's basic policy, as stated in the tanshin, is to promote the optimisation of management resources and the strengthening of earning power and to strengthen the base for corporate-value enhancement, with a focus on capital efficiency through cash-allocation-based resource allocation and on capital profitability through strengthening core businesses and expanding growth businesses, alongside materiality (ESG) responses and DX promotion. The president's message adds the operating themes: a production system that fulfils global supply responsibility in high-purity phosphoric acid, resource separation and recycling plant in Machinery, and compound-semiconductor demand capture in Electronic Materials on accumulated rare-metal recycling technology.

What the plan does not contain — in any source used here — is numbers. No quantified mid-term financial plan exists for Rasa in the tanshin disclosure: no revenue, profit, margin, ROE or capex targets for FY3/28 or any later year are published, and the PL/segment sheet register records this explicitly (S8: 'No quantified mid-term management plan is disclosed in the tanshin; none has been invented or entered'). This report therefore does not present plan targets, and the only forward figures anywhere in it are the FY3/27 company guidance of Chapter 2. The one quantified growth investment in the sources is the Taiwan capacity expansion — about ¥3.0bn for about +40% capacity, started April 2026 (interview pack, from company materials via a secondary compilation; the tanshin does not itemise it, and its depreciation and utilisation are not disclosed) — consistent with the FY3/26 capex step-up to ¥4,373mn but not separately verifiable from the tanshin. The absence of a quantified plan is itself an initiation finding: after FY3/27, the equity story has no company-supplied anchor, and the Q3 print and any new mid-term plan announcement (the current plan ends with FY3/27) are the events that would create one.

Shareholder returns are dividend-only in the sources used. The dividend has risen every year since FY3/21 on the adjusted basis of Chapter 6 (¥9 → ¥14 → ¥16.4 → ¥18.2 → ¥24 → ¥36), the FY3/26 payout ratio was 32.2% as reported (DOE 4.7%), and the FY3/27 forecast of ¥43 (interim ¥18, year-end ¥25) was raised alongside guidance on 4 November 2026 — a payout of about 32% of guided EPS of ¥133.08 (calculated). No buyback is recorded in the periods covered here (treasury shares were 646,030 at September 2026, broadly flat). The monitoring set that substitutes for a fuller plan, in the order the data arrives: H2 delivery against the implied ¥3,937mn of H2 operating profit (calculated), with Q3 cumulative progress the first checkpoint; Chemicals' semiconductor-related sales ratio against the 51.1% FY3/26 base and any disclosure of the Taiwan plant's ramp; Electronic Materials' growth rate against the +45.9% H1 print; the Other segment's H1 decline — stabilisation or trend; and the announcement (or continued absence) of a quantified successor plan to Mid-term Plan 2026. All forward figures above are company guidance, labelled as such; this report contains no J-Core Fundamental Research forecasts. Source: Q2 FY3/27 tanshin qualitative section, 11 November 2026; FY3/26 tanshin; PL/segment sheet register S8; interview pack.

blocks.heading: 8. Other information
blocks.html:
History. Rasa Industries traces to 1913, when its founder began phosphate-rock mining on Rasa Island (Oki-Daito Island) — the source of the company name — and was incorporated on 26 June 1918 (company president's message; incorporation date from the Gビズインフォ corporate registry entry, accessed November 2026). The group has since exited its founding businesses — fertiliser, mining, smelting and sulphuric acid — and today operates the Chemicals, Machinery and Electronic Materials businesses described in Chapter 3 (third-party summary, Wikipedia, accessed November 2026, flagged as such; the president's message confirms the current three-division structure and the century of phosphoric-acid technology). Head office: 1-18-13 Sotokanda, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo (EDINET filing header, June 2026). The shares are listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime Market.

Management. Representative Director, President and Executive Officer: Katsumasa Kitada (北田 勝誠) — named in that role in the Q1 FY3/27 tanshin (12 August 2026) and the Q2 FY3/27 tanshin (11 November 2026), and already named as representative in the company's EDINET extraordinary report of 26 June 2026. He succeeded Kosaku Sakao (坂尾 耕作), who is named as president in the FY3/26 tanshin (14 May 2026) and in the FY3/26 securities report (22 June 2026); the change therefore took effect around the June 2026 annual shareholders' meeting (the 158th AGM was held on 25 June 2026, per the extraordinary report). The inquiry contact in the Q2 FY3/27 tanshin is Atsushi Hayashi (林 敦), Director and Senior Executive Officer. (Romanisation of the president's given name follows the standard reading of 勝誠; the kanji and role are as printed in the tanshin and EDINET filings.)

Major shareholders. Not disclosed in the tanshin and not presented from a primary source here (未取得 from the sources used): a third-party compilation (Wikipedia, accessed November 2026) lists The Master Trust Bank of Japan (trust account) at 9.37%, Custody Bank of Japan (trust account) at 4.78% and a BNP Paribas Securities (Lux) fund account at 4.78% — third-party data of unstated date, flagged accordingly, with no controlling shareholder indicated. Employees: consolidated headcount is not disclosed in the tanshin (PL/segment sheet register S7) and is not presented here (未取得).

Shareholder returns. Dividends per share (adjusted basis, calculated) rose from ¥8 (FY3/18–FY3/20) to ¥36 in FY3/26, with the FY3/27 forecast raised to ¥43 on 4 November 2026 (interim ¥18; year-end ¥25) — a 3.4% yield at ¥1,259 (calculated) and a payout of about 32% of guided EPS. The FY3/26 dividend as reported (pre-split basis) was ¥180 per share (interim ¥64, year-end ¥116), a payout ratio of 32.2% and DOE of 4.7% (FY3/26 tanshin).

Market data. The shares closed at ¥1,259 on 16 November 2026 (FISCO price history via search results; corroborated by StockAnalysis.com), giving a market capitalisation of about ¥49.2bn (calculated from the cited price and the 39.07mn shares excluding treasury at September 2026; StockAnalysis.com shows ¥49.18bn). The 52-week range was ¥974 (19 November 2025) to ¥2,810 (4 June 2026) (Finnhub) — the shares had therefore fallen about 55% from the June 2026 peak into mid-November, including a sharp two-way November: the stock closed at ¥1,465 on 4 November (the guidance-raise date), fell to ¥1,182 on 6 November, recovered to ¥1,435 on 11 November (the Q2 print date) and eased to ¥1,259 by 16 November (FISCO). At ¥1,259 the shares trade at 11.3x FY3/26 basic EPS of ¥111.63 (post-split basis as restated in the FY3/26 tanshin), 9.5x FY3/27 company-guidance EPS of ¥133.08, and 1.5x FY3/26 book value per share of ¥815.15 (all calculated from the cited price and company-reported per-share data). The next scheduled disclosure is the Q3 FY3/27 tanshin, expected in February 2027 (third-party calendar estimate: 17 February 2027, Roic AI).

blocks.heading: 9. Basis of preparation
blocks.html:
Sources. Historical financials and segment data are taken from the PL/segment sheet for Rasa Industries (4022) (J-GAAP template; March year-end; ¥mn), built from the company's tanshin in the JPX disclosure archive. The copy used is the history-deepened copy at ~/workspace/pl-segment/work/h8out/recalc_hist8/4022_Rasa_PL.xlsx (LibreOffice-recalculated, data-only values read), which carries ten annual years — the main window FY3/22–FY3/26 (tabs 'PL & Key Drivers', 'Quarterly calculation', 'Segments', 'Operating metrics', 'Drivers', 'Reported inputs') plus the supplementary history block FY3/17–FY3/21 in 'Reported inputs' rows 112–160 — in preference to the five-year copy in the company's own work folder (~/workspace/pl-segment/work/rasa/recalc/), whose main-window figures agree with it. Sheet register S1–S13 (main window) and S10–S13 (history block); rollout log batch 6a (build, 2026-11-16) and history wave H8 (deepening, 2026-11-17); all template checks equal zero with documented rounding plugs (≤¥4mn main window, ≤¥2mn history block). Q1 and Q2 FY3/27 figures are from the Q1 FY3/27 tanshin dated 12 August 2026 and the Q2 FY3/27 tanshin dated 11 November 2026 (local copies in the sheet work folder). Guidance history is from the guidance tracker dated 17 November 2026, verified against the FY3/26 tanshin (initial guidance, 14 May 2026) and the Q2 tanshin (current guidance). The interview pack for 4022 (data as of 16 November 2026) is used for the securities-report figures it carries (semiconductor-related sales, largest customer) and for the Taiwan expansion item, each flagged at use. There is NO English transcript for 4022 in the programme's transcript library, and no Q&A is cited. Market data are from FISCO, Finnhub and StockAnalysis.com as returned by web search on 17 November 2026 and are cited with dates in the text; the president's identity was confirmed against the tanshin and an EDINET extraordinary report (26 June 2026) via web search.

Discrepancies and basis breaks flagged (not silently resolved). (1) Receivables correction: the h8out sheet copy's annual receivables cells (FY3/23–FY3/26) held only the electronically recorded claims line of each year's balance sheet (¥1,034mn / ¥1,303mn / ¥1,114mn / ¥2,054mn) and the FY3/22 annual cell was blank; the programme's F-C2 fix (register entry S14, 17 November 2026) corrected them to the full sums — FY3/22 ¥10,377mn, FY3/23 ¥11,302mn, FY3/24 ¥12,231mn, FY3/25 ¥11,664mn, FY3/26 ¥11,851mn — and this report uses the corrected values. The following year's quarterly tanshin print the prior year-end combined receivables line ¥1mn above the annual split sums (source rounding; the annual split sums stand). (2) Guidance wording: the sheet register (S8) describes FY3/27 guidance as 'unchanged at Q2 FY2027', while the tracker and the interview pack record a revision on 4 November 2026; both are reconciled in Chapter 2 — the Q2 tanshin carried the 4 November revised figures unchanged (修正の有無：無 is relative to that notice), and the revision chain in this report follows the tracker and the notices. (3) Interview pack versus tanshin: the pack marks the H1 FY3/27 segment split 未取得 (it was compiled from the tanshin summary), but the full Q2 tanshin segment note discloses it — this report uses the tanshin note; the pack's Q1 FY3/27 operating profit of ¥1,810mn (from a secondary compilation) differs from the Q1 tanshin's ¥1,805mn — this report uses ¥1,805mn; the pack's FY3/26 segment figures from briefing materials are rounded (Machinery profit ¥410mn vs tanshin ¥405mn; Electronic Materials sales ¥2,400mn vs ¥2,395mn; Chemicals profit ¥5,530mn vs ¥5,531mn) — this report uses the tanshin/sheet figures. (4) Segment adjustments: the printed corporate adjustments differ from the sheet's tie-out adjustments by ¥1mn in FY3/25 (printed −¥1,232mn vs sheet −¥1,231mn) and FY3/26 (printed −¥1,367mn vs sheet −¥1,366mn), and in the history block the printed adjustments (−¥864mn / −¥897mn / −¥930mn for FY3/18/19/21) differ from the sheet's formula values (−¥863mn / −¥895mn / −¥928mn) by ¥1mn–¥2mn — rounding plugs under register S9/S12; headline lines are always as reported. (5) Per-share breaks: share counts break twice — the 10-for-1 consolidation of 1 October 2017 (FY3/17 figures are on the pre-consolidation basis as reported, 79,287,093 weighted shares) and the 5-for-1 split of 1 April 2026 (FY3/25 EPS as originally reported was ¥398.74; the FY3/26 tanshin restates it to ¥79.75 on the split-adjusted basis, and restates share counts back to the start of FY3/25). Exhibit 1 and Chapter 6 therefore present EPS and dividends per share on a calculated split/consolidation-adjusted basis, labelled as calculated; as-reported figures are given in Chapter 6's notes where they differ. The sheet's own weighted-share row mixes bases across the break (FY3/26: 39.052153mn on the restated basis against 7.9mn-scale figures for FY3/22–25 as originally reported) and is not used directly. (6) FY3/17 tax: the −¥749mn deferred-tax credit makes FY3/17 net income exceed profit before tax (as reported; flagged in Chapters 1 and 6).
